ul.li: 3.0 and 2.0 share one transaction. The DFD cannot express this, but the number allocation, the ticket write, the audit entry, and the outbox row all commit together or not at all. Two staff encoding at the same second is the case this protects against — see design doc §3.2 and 02-ticket-number-sequence.d2.
7.0 is asynchronous. It is triggered by D6, not by an actor, and its failure never blocks 2.0 or 5.0 (FR-26). This is why D6 exists at all rather than 2.0 calling Google directly.
The sheet returns no ticket data (FR-22) — only acknowledgements and errors.

5.0 writes a status; it never deletes a row. There is no Voided status and no delete path — deletion would gap the sequence in D4 and orphan a row already sent to the sheet. Mis-encoded tickets are corrected by editing, and 6.0 records it.

2.0 can write any of the three statuses directly. The department fixes the concern first and records it after, so most tickets are created already Closed. Open and Ongoing are entered at creation only when that is what actually happened.
D7 is empty until OPEN-4 is answered by the IT team.
